newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bill volume down, rate up at Croatian bank auction.
newsitem.headline: Bill volume down, rate up at Croatian bank auction.

text.p: Bill volume shrank to only 57 million kuna on Wednesday from 150 million at Croatia's central bank weekly auction as commercial banks battled poor liquidity.
The central bank received only two bids for its five-week bills and issued them at 8.0 percent, one basis point higher than last Wednesday, an official told Reuters.
Market participants said a new increase of interbank rates to between 9.0 and 12 percent this week, following a long decline, made loan business more attractive again than bills.
The additional mandatory reserve payment on Wednesday, expected to drain almost 130 million kuna from the banking sector, also prevented larger investor interest.
Central bank bill auctions are not open to foreigners.
